title: chgrp
definition: Change Group. A command specifically used to change the group ownership of a file or directory, without affecting the user ownership.
simpleExplanation: Changing which team is allowed to use a file, without changing the individual who owns it.
realWorldExample: You create a project file. You want your entire engineering team to be able to edit it. You run `chgrp engineers project.txt`.
useCases: Managing team access to shared folders

intermediate: Can a normal user change a file's group to a group they are NOT a member of?

answers.question: Why rarely used?
answers.answer: Because the `chown` command can change both the user and the group at the exact same time (e.g., `chown user:group`), making `chgrp` somewhat redundant.

answers.question: Change to external group?
answers.answer: No. A regular user can only change a file's group to a group they are actively a member of.
